investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state and the eval timed out before any VM was assigned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state. This prevents the eval runner from reaching the createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) and producing any evidence, causing a complete contract gap for all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=145669, confirming the eval ran to its timeout without producing any evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 142s, no evidence keys — all three checks share the same scheduling failure root.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible. If those 2 nodes lose capacity, the entire pool is blocked.
Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource; if demand exceeds the slot count on those 2 nodes there is no horizontal fallback.
Lower probability — a recent deployment increased the number of concurrent remote-agent pods beyond the available VM slot budget, exhausting capacity faster than pods are released.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was stuck unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state eval never reached the state-polling phase, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) empty.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry it. Of the six available nodes, the two kata-capable nodes report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and the other four do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the kata nodes and affinity mismatches are not preemptable. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable, preventing agent creation and making all downstream state-polling and runtime checks impossible. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state and the eval timed out before any VM was assigned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state. This prevents the eval runner from reaching the createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) and producing any evidence, causing a complete contract gap for all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod stuck unscheduled for 137s before eval gave up.
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=145669, confirming the eval ran to its timeout without producing any evidence.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — zero evidence keys were written, consistent with the pod never starting.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the runner never reached the agent-creation code path.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), pod stuck 143s, no evidence keys.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 142s, no evidence keys — all three checks share the same scheduling failure root.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call is never reached because the pod is unschedulable before any VM is assigned.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible. If those 2 nodes lose capacity, the entire pool is blocked.
Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource; if demand exceeds the slot count on those 2 nodes there is no horizontal fallback.
Lower probability — a recent deployment increased the number of concurrent remote-agent pods beyond the available VM slot budget, exhausting capacity faster than pods are released.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 137–143 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod never scheduled, no agent was created, and the remote-agent-runtime check produced zero evidence, violating all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request is immediately Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint in the production-api environment, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent(..., "remote", ...) at run-status-probes.mjs:1918, which submits a pod that never starts, so no runtime response is ever returned and all required evidence fields remain empty.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the pod-submission path that triggers the scheduler error.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — the feature is already in a degraded/outage state from the two required check failures alone.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, this would reduce effective capacity even if total VM slots are unchanged.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the 2 eligible nodes may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus live workloads, with no burst or preemption policy configured to handle overflow.
UNLIKELY — eval runner configuration error causing incorrect pod spec: possible but not supported by evidence; the scheduler message is specific to resource exhaustion, not a malformed request.

affectedAreas.label: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool — production cluster infrastructure
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the only 2 nodes eligible by affinity. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity boundary, not an application or eval configuration issue. Evidence: failed-check.message.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm slot availability on the 2 eligible production nodes using kubectl describe nodes. If slots are fully consumed, identify and terminate any stale or leaked remote-agent pods that are holding slots without active workloads.

Investigate whether the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector can be made eligible (e.g., by applying the required node labels) to increase the scheduling pool and reduce pressure on the 2 current nodes.

Review cluster capacity planning for kata.peerpods.io/vm: if the eval runner and live workloads compete for the same fixed VM slot pool, consider reserving a dedicated slot or namespace quota for observability eval pods.

Confirm the scope of this failure as an eval infrastructure issue, not a user-facing incident. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence. The check remote-agent-runtime is marked required=false; however, remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true and both failed, meaning the remote-agents feature has crossed the outageAfterFailures=2 threshold in the eval system.

After restoring capacity, re-run all three remote-agents checks to confirm recovery and validate that the expected-output contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are populated and the message assertion ('hello from aura') passes.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-runtime that returns a scheduled pod and populated evidence fields would disprove active capacity exhaustion.

kubectl describe nodes showing available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes would disprove the exhaustion hypothesis and shift focus to a pod spec or affinity misconfiguration.

A different scheduler error message (e.g., image pull failure, resource quota exceeded at namespace level, or admission webhook rejection) on re-run would indicate a different root cause than VM slot exhaustion.
Evidence that only one of the three sibling checks fails, or that failures occur on different node subsets, would weaken the shared-capacity-exhaustion hypothesis.
Confirmation that the 4 non-matching nodes previously matched the pod's affinity rules (i.e., label drift is new) would shift the primary cause from VM exhaustion to affinity misconfiguration.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector rules, alerting before capacity is fully exhausted.
Add a remote-agent pod scheduling latency eval with a tighter warning threshold (e.g., warn if scheduling takes longer than 30s) to catch capacity pressure before it causes full timeouts.

Consider a dedicated remote-agents capacity check that monitors the ratio of allocated to allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%).
